title: Indigenous Patient Safety Investigator and Advocate
focus: A culturally safer route for First Nations, Métis and Inuit patient concerns—and the public evidence still needed about its results
what_happened: Alberta created an Indigenous Patient Safety Investigator and Advocate within the Office of Alberta Health Advocates after an Indigenous advisory panel called for a more accountable response to racism and patient concerns. The role supports First Nations, Métis and Inuit patients and families, helps navigate complaint processes, can conduct a bounded Health Charter review where no other process exists, and can make recommendations to government and health authorities.
why_this_matters: It creates a distinct point of contact for First Nations, Métis and Inuit patients who encounter racism, mistreatment or other concerns in Alberta health care.
Its public authority is meaningful but limited: it can support, review and recommend, but cannot reverse decisions, discipline providers or impose penalties.
The role is operating, while aggregate complaint, outcome and system-change reporting remains difficult to locate publicly.
one_thing_to_remember: The office provides a documented complaint-support and review route, but the public record does not yet show a comprehensive account of its caseload, recommendations or resulting changes.

items.title: Located within a provincial office
items.text: The role is part of the Office of Alberta Health Advocates and the public job description places it in Alberta Health, reporting to the Manager, Investigations. Miller North therefore does not describe it as institutionally independent.

items.title: Delegated and bounded review authority
items.text: Where no other dispute-resolution process exists, the advocate may review—with or without a complaint—whether conduct was inconsistent with the Alberta Health Charter. The public page does not describe general coercive or disciplinary powers.

items.title: Community relationships are part of the mandate
items.text: The public mandate includes relationships with First Nations, Métis and Inuit representatives and leaders and access to Elders, Knowledge Keepers and Knowledge Holders. Public governance or oversight terms for those relationships were not located.

sources.title: Indigenous Patient Safety Investigator and Advocate

items.title: One aggregate activity measure is public
items.text: Alberta's 2026–29 business plan reports 321 correspondence items in 2025 for this role. That number measures correspondence, not unique complainants, accepted cases, completed reviews, recommendations or outcomes.

sources.title: Primary and Preventative Health Services Business Plan 2026–29

dossier_sections.title: From a concern to possible follow-up

items.title: 1. Contact and intake
items.text: A First Nations, Métis or Inuit patient or family member can contact the Office of Alberta Health Advocates. The office asks for a general description and warns people not to send a health number or detailed health information through the initial web form.

sources.title: Contact the Health Advocates

items.title: 2. Triage and navigation
items.text: An office representative determines how the concern can be addressed. The office may provide information, support early resolution or refer the person to another complaints body when the concern is outside its jurisdiction.

sources.title: Make a complaint to the Health Advocate offices
Indigenous Patient Safety Investigator job description

items.title: 3. Review where the mandate permits
items.text: If no other dispute process exists, delegated Health Charter review authority may apply. The advocate can also assist with investigations and make recommendations or provide system advice.

sources.title: Indigenous Patient Safety Investigator and Advocate
Indigenous Patient Safety Investigator job description

items.title: 4. Recommendation and follow-up
items.text: The mandate includes recommendations and advice to government, health authorities and professional organizations. A public procedure for responses, follow-up, reconsideration or appeals was not located in the sources reviewed.

sources.title: Indigenous Patient Safety Investigator and Advocate

items.title: Who it supports
items.text: The published mandate is for First Nations, Métis and Inuit patients and families with concerns about Alberta health-care services. The office is reachable by phone, email or the provincial web inquiry form.

sources.title: Indigenous Patient Safety Investigator and Advocate
Contact the Health Advocates

items.title: Published restrictions
items.text: The advocate cannot represent a person in court or at a tribunal, reverse a clinical or administrative decision, discipline a provider, impose fines or investigate federal or municipal governments, police, universities, schools or non-health companies.

sources.title: Indigenous Patient Safety Investigator and Advocate

items.title: Processes not publicly resolved
items.text: The pages reviewed do not set out a case-specific time limit, appeal route, reconsideration route or public reporting standard for this role. Those details should not be inferred.
